title: the-chart-refuses-proves-keys-that-disagree-with-the-falsifier-clauses
intention: The chart's validate door refuses a packet whose named proof declares PROVES teeth for the ticket under keys that disagree with the ticket's falsifier clause markers, so the disagreement is caught when the proof is first declared, not at PROVEME or clearance.
why: Law 4: a rule held as memory failed three times (50ad391f4e95, 693e9f45e6f2, 5f217a2d4bd6) — each time a proof's PROVES keys disagreed with the falsifier's clause markers and the disagreement surfaced only at hollow or clearance, where it costs a refusal, a FIXME bounce or a falsifier rewrite at PROVEME. The lived symptom is a builder who did the work and is stopped at the last gate by a key mismatch the chart could have named.
traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy: the memory rule failed n=3); Law 8 (a proof whose declared teeth do not map to the falsifier's clauses lets hollow read a build as measured when no declared tooth covers a clause); Law 1 (each slip re-derived the same fix at PROVEME)
how: In cairn/devices/codemother/machines/validate/validate.py inspect_validate(): add one inspected entry, 'proves_keys_match_the_falsifier_clauses', recorded only when the packet claims a ticket (an unclaimed chart has no falsifier to check against). The rule mirrors clearance's (proof_coverage.lacks, the union over named proofs, extra keys allowed), as Akien agreed in open-514724f8ec30 (recommendation a): take every distinct proof path named in the packet's criteria instruments (regex [\w./-]*/proofs/[\w./-]+\.py, resolved against root); want = proof_coverage.clauses(ticket_doc) with the ticket read through grammar.ticket_path; have = the union of proof_coverage.declared(proof).get(ticket, {}) keys over those proofs. The entry passes when want is a subset of have; it closes the gate when have is empty (no proof the chart runs declares the ticket) or some clause is missing, naming each proof with its declared keys, the clause keys, the missing clauses, and the one-line fix (key PROVES to the clauses, or have a criterion run the proof that does). proof_coverage is imported at call time through its public package interface (cairn.tools.proof_coverage). The check lives in inspect_validate only, never in the build inspector's judge_validate, so it fires at the write of a new validate berth and no standing berth is re-judged: the three standing PROVED charts it would refuse (7a1265439f54, a1a2156a2a17, a808e21d646f, census 2026-10-06) predate the rule and are not reopened. Proof under cairn/devices/codemother/machines/validate/proofs/, written red.
falsifier: Done when (1) a validate packet claiming a ticket whose falsifier has no (N) markers, with a criterion running a proof that declares PROVES {tid: {'1':..,'2':..}}, is refused naming proves_keys_match_the_falsifier_clauses, the declared keys ['1','2'] and the clauses ['all']; (2) a claimed packet whose proofs declare keys equal to the clauses passes that entry; (3) a claimed packet none of whose proofs declares anything for the ticket is refused; (4) a claimed packet whose clauses are covered only by the union of two proofs (clause 1 in one, clause 2 in the other) passes that entry. Wrong intent if the gate re-judges a standing validate berth: the census of 2026-10-06 measured 3 standing PROVED charts it would refuse, and Akien answered (open-514724f8ec30) that they predate the rule.
watchme: none, because the consumer is the next chart run: its validate berth under /home/akien/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets/ carries the proves_keys_match_the_falsifier_clauses entry, pass or fail, which is the measurement this ticket produces
children: none, because the change is one inspector entry in one machine with one proof
